name: Frederick Espinoza

summary.text: Frederick Espinoza owns and operates a small business. He says he fell behind academically in a traditional high school and was put on a path to work and small business through an alternative high school and Warren Tech.

experience.text: Served as an Access-a-Ride driver for disabled riders.

education_focus.text: Espinoza says his central issue is transparency: giving parents and taxpayers access to real proficiency data, curriculum, budgets, and notice on health and policy decisions.

On academic standards, he says the board should put 'grade-level literacy, mathematics, science, American history and civics, and financial literacy' back 'at the center' and that standards should say what students must know, 'not which identity conclusions to reach.'
He opposes using declining enrollment alone to deny charter-school applications, saying a charter appeal 'should turn on academics, safety, and finances — not on protecting a district's headcount.'

positions.source_title: 9 questions for Colorado's State Board of Education candidates this year
positions.quote: Amendment 87 is another tax-rule change sold as classroom funding. Keep officials accountable. Vote no.
positions.note: Part of his answer opposing both Proposition NN and Amendment 87.
